verdict: Ordinary immutable DAGs can represent the tested distinctions, but hashes alone do not provide occurrence uniqueness, complete provenance, or recovery/conflict guarantees.
counterexamples: Content-only execution records collapse two identical trials into one.
Repeated occurrence issuer/counter collapses distinct requests despite occurrence fields.
Incidental resolved outputs unnecessarily change naive closure identity.
Mutable URI-only names conceal artifact version changes.
One attempt can hide two actual external executions unless the executor reports both.
Last-writer status overwrites simultaneous lifecycle observations.
priority_gaps: P0: dispatch/accounting evidence and durable publication boundaries
P0: closure binding projection and artifact integrity
P1: transactional head CAS, occurrence allocation, and lifecycle reconciliation
P1: retirement/result availability versus true tombstones and sensitive erasure
P2: policy registry, validation, adoption defaults, and merge rationale
limitations: HCL is opaque stored text; resource resolution is synthetic, not OpenTofu evaluation.
External execution, cleanup and deletion are simulations/assertions.
Crash recovery uses injected exceptions and object re-instantiation, not process termination or power loss.
Concurrent publication uses deterministic interleaving, not multiprocess transactions.
No production DML compatibility, physical erasure, or exactly-once guarantee established.
next_experiment: Kill two local drivers at effect/commit boundaries with a non-idempotent durable mock executor, then repeat with idempotency and transactional head updates.
